dive: 'one NVIDIA graphics chip holds up to 76B of them' is out of date. The 76B ceiling is NVIDIA's Sep 2022 figure for Ada Lovelace (confirmed on nvidia.com), but newer NVIDIA chips are bigger: the RTX 5090's GB202 has about 92.2B (PC Gamer, hwcooling) and data-centre Blackwell dies have more. Stated today, 'up to 76B' is wrong. Fix: tie it to its chip and year, e.g. 'one NVIDIA graphics chip from 2022 holds up to 76B of them', or re-source a current count.

flow: 'A tiny current into one contact lets a far bigger one through the other' misstates how the point-contact transistor worked. The source (CHM) says 'the voltage on one contact modulated the current flowing through the other'. Its current gain was small (about 1 to 3); the 100x gain was in signal strength, not one current against the other. Expert viewers will catch it (profile: accuracy over spectacle). Fix: e.g. 'A small voltage on one contact controls the current through the other.' Redraw the flow visuals (thin cyan trickle vs thick amber stream) to match.
